title: Replace global scheduler lock with work-stealing queues and epochal KV snapshots
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Background: The current global scheduler uses a coarse-grained mutex to coordinate slot allocation, prefetch, and batch commit across tenants. This has repeatedly shown up in p50->p99 regressions under multi-tenant bursty workloads and makes incremental refactors risky due to contention hotspots. The KV cache currently exposes a monolithic snapshot API which blocks cache writers during compaction cycles, amplifying tail latency.

Proposal: Replace the single global scheduler lock with a set of per-worker work-stealing queues and a lightweight, epoch-based coordination layer. Introduce epochal KV snapshots (shard-local, copy-on-write metadata only) to allow compactions and warmup to proceed without pausing the hot-path writers. At a high level: 1) implement a lock-free enqueue path for the common fast-case (single producer or local worker), 2) add work-stealing logic for idle workers to claim tasks from overloaded neighbors, 3) introduce an epoch manager that publishes new KV snapshot handles atomically and retires old epochs once no in-flight batches reference them.

Why this is different from previous attempts: earlier refactors broken down the batcher but retained the centralized lease manager and blocking snapshot path. This ticket aims for a cohesive migration plan that is incremental and reversible with feature flags (scheduler.work_steal_enabled, kv.epochal_snapshots).
success_criteria: 1) p99 scheduler lock contention metric (scheduler.global_lock_wait_ms) reduced by >80% in synthetic multi-tenant benchmark; 2) end-to-end p99 latency reduction >= 25% for 512-token long-running sessions; 3) no increase in token cost beyond 2%; 4) can toggle new scheduler off without request loss; 5) KV snapshot GC does not exceed memory budget in steady state.
milestones: M1: Prototype work-stealing queue and lock-free enqueue (branch: feat/ws-queue) - 2w
M2: Integrate epoch manager and lightweight snapshot handle for KV - 2w
M3: End-to-end integration tests + canary on internal staging with traffic split 5% - 1w
M4: Performance tuning and dependency upgrades (tokio 1.0->1.12, crossbeam upgrade) - 1w
M5: Gradual rollout to production with monitoring + rollback playbook - 1w
plan: - Week 1: build prototype queue and microbench against current mutex path. - Week 2: implement epoch manager and adapt KV shard code to return epoch handles instead of blocking snapshots. - Week 3: add metrics (lock wait histogram, epoch retention duration, steal events), run chaos tests and memory regression tests. - Week 4: upgrade runtime deps used by scheduler (async runtime and atomic/sharded structures) and validate on staging. - Week 5: canary rollout and collect perf/ops signals, then full rollout if metrics pass.
benchmarks_and_results: Initial microbench (local) shows lock-free enqueue increases throughput by 1.6x under 96-worker contention. Early snapshot prototype reduced writer stall time from 12ms to <0.5ms per compaction cycle in a synthetic KV churn test. Full multi-tenant benchmark results will be posted after M3.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: Work-stealing introduces non-deterministic scheduling path that can affect QoS for latency-sensitive tenants. Mitigation: add tenant-level fairness token and bound steals per epoch. - Risk: Epochal snapshots might increase live metadata memory. Mitigation: conservative default retention and adaptive GC thresholds per shard; add KV.memory_retention_limit flag. - Risk: Dependency upgrades (tokio/crossbeam) could surface hidden regressions. Mitigation: isolate upgrades behind feature flags and run full test matrix in CI.
testing_plan: Unit tests for queue correctness, property-based tests for epoch retirement, load test harness that replays production traces, blue-green canary with 5/20/50% splits and automatic rollback conditions defined (latency/regression thresholds). Add fuzzing for corner cases of concurrent snapshot retire. CI must run with both old and new flags enabled to check interoperability.
rollout: Feature-flagged rollout controlled by scheduler.work_steal_enabled and kv.epochal_snapshots. Start with staging cluster replica, then internal canary (5% traffic) for 48h, expand to 20% if stable, then 100% after 72h stable metrics. Rollback via feature toggle if p95 latency increases >10% or errors increase beyond historical baseline.
operational_runbook: - Dashboard: scheduler.global_lock_wait_ms, kv.epoch_retention_secs, steal_success_rate, batch_retries, p99_latency. - Immediate action: disable scheduler.work_steal_enabled and kv.epochal_snapshots flags. - If memory spike: throttle compaction with kv.compaction_rate_limit. - Postmortem steps: capture heap profile and epoch references snapshot, correlate with steal events.
notes: This ticket bundles a moderate surface-area change and a deps upgrade. Keep change small and observable. Prefer feature-flagged behavior and clear metrics before full cutover. Coordinate with SRE for canary windows and set up a dedicated rollback Slack channel.
